appraisal_events.evidence: ces joies... je les goûtais au contraire pendant qu'Albertine n'était pas auprès de moi... que d'ailleurs je ne trouvais plus guère jolie et avec laquelle je m'ennuyais, que j'avais la sensation nette de ne pas aimer
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator states plainly that he no longer finds Albertine pretty, is bored in her company, and clearly senses that he does not love her; his true joys now come only in her absence, a sharp reversal from the earlier intimacy.

appraisal_events.evidence: Elle trouvait bizarre, choquant, qu'une jeune fille habitât seule avec moi... elle l'était devenue depuis que... le séjour de la jeune fille se prolongeait chez nous... Cette hostilité, je ne peux pourtant pas dire que ma mère me la manifestât jamais.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's mother privately regards Albertine's prolonged, unchaperoned residence as improper and grows quietly hostile to the arrangement, though scruple keeps her from ever voicing the reproach directly.

appraisal_events.evidence: C'est Françoise qui lui imposa ces règles... celle-ci comprit avec stupeur qu'elle se trouvait dans un monde étrange, aux coutumes inconnues, réglé par des lois de vivre qu'on ne pouvait songer à enfreindre... n'essaya même pas de résister et attendit patiemment chaque matin mon coup de sonnette pour oser faire du bruit.
appraisal_events.explanation: Françoise, steeped in the household's tradition of exacting deference for its master, imposes strict rules of silence on Albertine, who submits completely and without resistance — a visible reversal in which the servant's authority outranks the young woman the narrator intends to marry.

appraisal_events.evidence: grâce à la bonté, au dévouement de Legrandin qui, ne reculant devant aucune peine, ajourna de semaine en semaine son retour à Paris... il sentit que la malade, condamnée, aimait ses soins et ne pouvait se passer de lui. Le snobisme est une maladie grave de l'âme, mais localisée et qui ne la gâte pas tout entière.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator credits Legrandin's genuine kindness and devotion in caring for the dying great-aunt, repeatedly delaying his own return to Paris, explicitly noting that his habitual snobbery is only a localized flaw that does not spoil his character entirely.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator explicitly withdraws desire and affection, stating he no longer finds her attractive, is bored by her, and does not love her; his happiness now depends on her absence rather than her presence.
The mother's private, largely unspoken disapproval of Albertine's residence marks a mild but real diminishment in how Albertine is regarded, even though it is never voiced to her directly.
Françoise's authority over household order is shown prevailing even over Albertine, confirming her traditional command within the house.
Albertine is shown wholly submitting to Françoise's household rules, waiting passively each morning rather than asserting her own position, a visible subordination within the home's hierarchy.
Legrandin is locally redeemed by his sustained, selfless devotion to the dying aunt, credited by the narrator as genuine kindness despite his habitual snobbery.
